ANSWER:
The restriction is enforced at save time through two functions in `pkg/okf/`:

1. **`pkg/okf/provenance.go` — `IsHumanIdentity(id string) bool`** (lines 9–18)
   The single classifier that defines "human actor." Only the exact string `"human"`, or strings beginning with `"human:"` or `"human/"`, return `true`. An actor like `"agent/mcp"` returns `false`.

2. **`pkg/okf/provenance.go` — `ensureNoForgedHumanVerification(fullPath string, c *Concept, actor string, isNew bool) error`** (lines 20–58)
   The core enforcement function. When the actor is not human (i.e., `IsHumanIdentity(actor)` is `false`), it reads the existing on-disk concept (if any) to collect already-recorded human verifications. If the concept being saved introduces any `Verified.By` entry that satisfies `IsHumanIdentity` and was not already on disk, it returns an error: `"actor %q cannot add human verification %q"`. The comment explicitly names the MCP server as the target of this guard.

3. **`pkg/okf/mutate.go` — `saveConceptLocked(bundleDir string, c *Concept, opts SaveOptions) error`** (lines 476–496)
   The single save path all writes flow through. It calls `ensureNoForgedHumanVerification` before any disk write; if the guard returns an error, the concept is never persisted.

The MCP server always passes `Actor: "agent/mcp"` in `SaveOptions` (`pkg/okf/mcp.go`, lines 647–653 and 749–754), which never satisfies `IsHumanIdentity`, so any attempt by the MCP server to add a human verification entry is rejected before the file is written.

CONFIDENCE: high
